utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Speigel and Solana are epidemiologists. Physicians for Human Rights conducted a quite different epidemiological study that was conducted early in the conflict, mid to -- mid-April. Both estimates are consistent with ours. Neither estimate measures precisely the same thing, the same period or the same deaths exactly that ours do, but our broad confidence intervals all agree with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thanks. You were asked a lot of questions about addendum 2, and it might well be that you're -- you have explained all there is to explain about it. When I say addendum 2, I mean your last addendum. May I just try to summarise what I think you're saying just to confirm, if possible, or to clear up any ambiguities that might exist in respect to what was said about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me. Your Honour, none of us remember asking any questions about addendum 2. We just had a little brief conference here. I don't think any of us did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry. I meant the addendum of the 28th of January, 2007, which is the second addendum that he produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That was certainly explored. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You produced this addendum at our request to incorporate new data that is available to the OTP. This is what you said in chief. However, you also produced table 1 because when you were previously here you had been requested by the -- you had been requested in the course of your testimony to produce it.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: However, apart from that, it is your view that it is because of its limitation not a useful tool to do the sort of analysis that you did in the principal work.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Because -- and if I may give you three reasons and ask you to comment. One, it measures only one peak not a flow over a period of time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And two, for a variety of reasons, you made it ultimate conservative which you have explained in that report.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what you're saying is that even if all of the boxes had inconclusive or coincides, it would not be a tool that could be used for the analysis that we are concerned about here or that is the subject of your principal report.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: There would still be substantial questions to be asked about the moments during which they were not peaks, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In fact, in your substantive report, you have in the appendices done -- breakdowns of municipalities and you also preceded, generally speaking, with a breakdown of the country into four regions and that is reflected in figure 3 of the substantive report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And also if you look at the charts at page 59 and page 60, you have analysed the regions, the flows in the regions --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really apologise, but we cannot follow who asked what in the cross-examination. So if our learned friend could point out in the transcript which part is he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, it's getting too complicated for me. We're going to have to adjourn now and resume after lunchtime if this has to be done in this sort of detail. I'm now confused, where I thought I was clear, and I need to ask some questions in any event. So we're going to go on for longer than we anticipated. I'm sorry about that, Dr. Ball. I thought we could finish this, but we can't. So could you please leave and we'll be resuming at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So back to where we broke off. We were going back to questions you were asked about the graphs on page 59 and 60 which explain the flows and your analysis in respect to the regions and which showed the flow -- correlations of KLA activity and NATO activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just find the precise quotation from the transcript for that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Right. You said in -- these graphs took us to the heart of the matter in explaining these flows, and you said that there are some anomalies, some of which are discussed in the text, and that what I want to ask you about. The question is this: Having regard to that, to what I just showed you and those graphs, do these anomalies impact on the results and could you explain without making it complicated very briefly why they do not.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they do not impact the results. As we discussed in the original report, the single most interesting anomaly is in the refugee flow in the eastern region where the residual pattern crosses. It reverses the pattern of the original data, indicating that there is perhaps some kind of influence of KLA or NATO activity at that point in that region. utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. And that's an example of the anomalies that you were discussing?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you just circle "Morina," please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. Nothing further. Could this -- before I sit, I'm reminded that -- could this be given an IC number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be IC123, Your Honours. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Dr. Ball, I wonder if you could answer the following questions, please, as precisely as you can. We were told that the January 28th, 2007, report was written on the instructions of the Office of the Prosecutor. Can you tell me, please, what these instructions were.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked me to do two broad things. First, they asked me to follow-up the questioning that I believe originated from Judge Kwon in the Milosevic trial, which led to -- in which he asked specifically for us to break down by municipality what were then, I believe, figures 8 and 9 in the original report. Let me refer to them to make sure I've got them just right. Those figures showed in summary form the discussions that we've been having about this issue of peaks and valleys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's sufficient for --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For that point.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There must have been more to the instruction than that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The second point that I was asked to investigate would be the impact of potential additional data that was not available when we did the 2002 report, but has become available since. There were four data sets I was asked to look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've got that. So these were the two things you were instructed to do?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, I said I think when you were giving evidence in chief that I hadn't grasped that part of the message in this new report was that it had inadequacies, and I'm still having difficulty accepting that that point is being made to us. If you could look at it, please. You have a hard copy there, do you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If I may have a moment to find it. Here we go. Which in specific do you want to look at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Look first at the beginning, the executive summary, the first paragraph, the second line you'll see the words: "We confirm and expand upon the results presented in 2002."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "We describe a revised and expanded analysis of the potential causal relationship between KLA or NATO activity and the subject we are dealing with."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You then say that: "We discuss how our coding scheme was intentionally conservative to provide the strongest possible test of the claims," so presumably that's a reference back to 2002 also. You then in the next section, in the third line, you say that in both the 2002 and the present report you consider three hypotheses and you say what these are. And then in the next paragraph you say: "If KLA activity or NATO air-strikes occur immediately before or during periods," plural, "of high levels of killing and migration, these events may plausibly be the cause of the rise and fall pattern." So that's a reference to the pattern which emerged in the original report. And then if you go over the page you talk in the first full paragraph over the page that -- about the current analysis showing no discernible causal relationship. And then you say: "Because the data coding process was automated for the 2007 analysis, the analysis reached slightly different conclusions about a few peaks; however, none of these recategorisations alters the conclusions." The next paragraph: "The procedure used in the current report was analogous to the procedure followed in 2002; however, to further increase precision the analysis was automated." And then skipping down to the last paragraph on that page: "As noted above, the 2007 analysis is consistent with the conclusions of the original 2002 analysis." We then have table 1 and then in the next page after that, third line in the graphs presented -- well, you're referring to the graphs presented and you state what emerges from some of these. And then in the next section, revaluating the effect of the coding rules you say: "Both the 2002 and 2007 analysis used conservative coding rules." If you go to the next paragraph, the third line: "Peaks towards the end of the period are thus more likely to be labelled as inconclusive."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And when I look at the various graphs there, they don't just have one peak; they have a number of peaks. And it was being suggested that this analysis that was carried out in this report was confined to a single peak and thus less inadequate, quite contradicting, I would suggest, the way in which the reader is likely to understand the import of this report. Now, would you like to comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would first like to say that I apologise for any confusion that may have been caused by that. Our comments here -- unfortunately we've got a bit of blinders because we're focussed very, very tightly in this discussion on the few paragraphs that surround figure 8 and 9 in the original report. So all of our discussion about confirming earlier hypotheses have to do with the conclusions we made with respect to those particular figures which are being expanded upon here. That said, and as I've said throughout the last two days, our preference very strongly is for any statistical conclusions to be made on other grounds not necessarily -- not on these peaks and valleys analysis but rather on the graphs and residuals analysis -- the regressions and residuals analysis that we discussed earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it not ultimately boil down to peaks and valleys, too?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does but it boils down to peaks and valleys in a much more finally grained way that takes into account both the presence of the putative causal phenomenon and the putative results together and their absences. And what this -- I mean -- excuse me, what this method lacks is the ability to consider what happens then there are no putative causes or putative results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, do you agree with me that it was unfortunate that these limitations were not highlighted in this report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, sir. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do know that this is rather unusual, but by your leave, I just wanted to pose one question to the witness concerning the map shown by Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Visnjic:

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]

utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it's not something that's said in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, you can ask that, Mr. Ackerman. Further cross-examination by Mr. Ackerman:

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Dr. Ball, like some other graphs we were looking at yesterday, because of the numbers from each of these regions that you were dealing with, the scales of each of these four graphs differ in some cases significantly. utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at the west graph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see around maybe the 8th or 9th or 10th of April a dip that doesn't correspond. Right after that a kind of a trough that doesn't correspond.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you go and you see these and -- is it your position that these are not anomalies?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The anomaly that is of interest is the point at which the lines cross each other in opposite directions. They go apart from each other, that they diverge from each other, is interesting, but only interesting insofar as the error would support that they are truly different. Again, these are estimates and we must be concerned about spurious differences. utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That clarifies it because when I -- what I understood as the anomaly was that large dip after where they cross each other. utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour. Thank you for leave to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Further questions by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Well, I acknowledge and appreciate your expertise and skills on the subject. Obviously, as I understand, that you were given data and those you used empirically in the process of statistical evaluation and we got the end result, and on which you had a command to tell us all what you have been doing. But the question is: Did you verify the data or it appeared truthful? Whatever. I mean, just try to -- that's all.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK BALL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's a great question. I -- as I said to some similar questions, yours is a subtler question, but to some similar questions earlier I said I did not conduct field investigations so I have not verified the data in the sense of going to the field and confirming individual stories; however, at a statistical level, we have confirmed the data or verified the data or done sanity checks on the data is the term that statisticians would use. And a sanity check would have the following feeling. We would say: For example, when we're looking at lots of data sets that describe the same events, do we see a distribution of repeated discussions of the same events. Do we see the kind of clustering around events that we would expect. If people were, for example, committing some sort of wholesale perjury in these stories, we would expect them to not converge at all. They would tell stories. It would be very, very hard. It's an immensely complex task to coordinate them so that two people told one story and a third person told a separate story and then four, five, and six persons told a combined story. That starts to require a tremendous amount of coordination. Instead, when we think about wholesale fabrication, we think of people going in and making things up, and we did not see that. And that's one way that we would, at a statistical level, look for large-scale fabrications. A second way we concerned ourselves about the veracity of the data was simply to ask the counter-factual question which is: What would happen to our results if some fraction of the data were, in fact, false. And So what we did was systematically perturb the underlying data. We just switched it all around. We made it lies and then we reran the analysis repeatedly as a kind of sensitivity analysis to falsification. Again - and this is found most in "Policy or Panic." There's a little bit of it in what the Prosecutors called the Principal Report. We found very little change in the results. We find the results to be very robust to what was told to us. This is what I was trying to explain earlier when I said that data analysis is like listening to a voice in a crowded room, that if you can make out the voice, external noise in the room does not necessarily change your ability to hear the voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness K88, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecution on 16th and 17th April 2005 and on 21st January 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could the witness please be handed a copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you look at the statement and please confirm whether this was the statement you provided to the Office of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you recently had the opportunity to review your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in the course of reviewing your statement, did you make two minor corrections which you pointed out to me during our proofing session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: One correction that you pointed out in proofing was that the last phrase of paragraph 3 should be deleted, starting with the words "my official title was" until the end of that sentence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The second correction you indicated in proofing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. I've -- the last -- this is paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is paragraph 3 and it's the last sentence. The phrase that starts with the words: "My official title was."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, thank you. The last line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The last line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The second correction you made in proofing was at paragraph 14, line 6 you indicated that the following phrase should be deleted: "And I had modified and made it usable again." This is in the middle of paragraph 14, line 6. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, K88. Other than those two minor corrections, after having reviewed your statement, are you satisfied that this statement accurately reflects to the best of your knowledge and recollection the truth about the events that are described in the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender the statement under seal. This is P2691.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like to inquire with the Court whether in this case we would need to provide a redacted statement. This has not yet been uploaded in e-court basically because -- basically -- I'm sorry. Because in the process of carrying out these redactions we noticed that substantive portions would have to be redacted in order to protect this witness's identity, and I'm not sure that the information that will remain if we carry out these redactions will be very meaningful or useful to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I think it's P2681. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I think what you should do is let the Trial Chamber see the redacted version so that we can decide whether it's appropriate to publish it in that form.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'll advise the Court when this has been uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I think it will be later today. I would like to show the witness the attachment to his statement, this is the B/C/S version, and would ask that this not be broadcasted outside the courtroom. This is page 11 of his B/C/S statement. There's no equivalent in the English. I see the English is being opened. And when this comes up could we please rotate it to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness K88, I understand from your statement that this is a map you drew for OTP investigators to explain the evidence that you describe in your statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In paragraph 14 of your statement you refer to a truck, to a FAP truck which you say that you observed at the base in early April 1999 when you went there. I would like you to point out where this truck is -- has been depicted on this map that you have drawn. If you could draw a circle around it just for clarity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the English version of this statement, this has incorrectly marked as 1V. It should be number 4 on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On mine it's number 6 in paragraph 14. Is that right? Or is it a later -- are we talking about some --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It's later down towards the middle of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, IV just means 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It just means 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: On this map you have drawn an arrow, a long arrow, towards the right of the circle that you just made, a number 4. Could you please explain what is depicted by that arrow that you have drawn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: There is a line that goes to the right of number 4, which you have drawn on this map, and I am just asking if you could indicate what that line indicates.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: That line shows the direction as to where the corpses from that truck were buried.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page, page 12. We have to give it an IC number under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC124 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Witness K88, what is depicted here by the number 1 that you have drawn towards the left of this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: That's grave number 1, that first one from the mentioned truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this grave that we're looking at located outside the area that you had drawn on your map, the previous page of the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, the previous drawing was a drawing of the firing range and between there is a parapet about 12 metres tall I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Would this first grave then be located outside the firing range area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, outside the firing range area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And can you explain who, if you know -- under whose control fell this area where the first grave was dug?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, roughly we used that area, too, although - how should I put this? - it was afforested at the time, or rather, it was covered with some kind of bush. It wasn't really used for anything, but it was under our control because after that there is a fence and then the PKB, the agricultural combine farm of Belgrade; it's owned by them, that land.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we return to page 11 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 14 you also mentioned seeing two further trucks which I understand are depicted here by 2V and 3V right under the number 4 you had drawn before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: At paragraph 16 you referred to these two trucks and you say that you saw them and then they left the base, and you say: "I later heard they also contained bodies but never saw the trucks again." Could you explain from whom you heard that these trucks numbered 2 and 3 also contained bodies.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, a colleague of ours, since we had been dislocated, he toured this area, this centre, from time to time and he looked a bit more closely and he probably came to this conclusion on the basis of the smell, and I don't know what else, that there were corpses inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did this person tell you anything about what happened to these trucks after they left the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: No. Just one moment. He probably just stopped by. I can't even remember who it was from among the men who were in charge of security at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. At paragraph 22 you referred to a fourth truck that you saw on the base -- that are different base some days later. Would this be what you have depicted as 4B to the bottom left-hand side of -- left-hand corner of your map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where would this be depicted on your map, the fourth truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: The fourth truck, 4V, in the lower left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking if that is where you indicated that you had seen this truck, what you have depicted there in the lower left-hand corner of your map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, but that was after all of this had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Would you describe the drivers of these truck -- of this fourth truck as having a Montenegrin accent and you said they were dressed in blue camouflage uniform, probably re service. And at paragraph 24 you said that after this truck had been emptied, the contents of this truck had been emptied, they had to go back to Kosovo. Could you explain how did you know that these truck drivers had to return to Kosovo. Is this something they told you themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, probably they said so. I don't remember exactly now. It's been a long time and a lot of things have happened, but I think they were the ones who told me that they were going back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say they had to return to Kosovo, did they tell you from where they had come? Had they originated -- that their journey from Kosovo? Is that what they had said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell us where they had come from or where they were returning. They did not refer to a specific place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you say in paragraph 24 that they had to go back to Kosovo. What do you mean by that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, probably, that is where they had come from, from down there, since most of the war events were taking place in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what made you assume that they had come from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, probably the way in which they spoke or I don't know exactly what to say now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. At paragraph 29 of your statement you talk about two further trucks, truck 5 and 6, and you describe the truck drivers as being an old man in civilian clothes and two others in police uniform. These two policemen that came with the fifth and sixth truck, are these different than the ones you saw with the fourth truck that you depicted on your map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes, they were different ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you say in the same paragraph that you didn't know where they were from, maybe Kosovo, they spoke Serbian. What made you think that these policemen and this man with this fifth and sixth truck came also from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why I thought that. They probably said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. At paragraph 30 of your statement you speak about the drivers on the second time that told you that while they were on their way to Belgrade, they had an accident and around 50 bodies had fallen out of the truck. When you say the drivers on the second time, are you referring to the drivers of truck number 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly now which truck was which, roughly, but it was their story, that is what they said, that that is what happened to them on the way, that the truck door had opened and that they started falling out, and ultimately they had a problem with the truck itself. The truck broke down once it had reached our base.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did they explain to you why they were transporting bodies on their -- in their truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we can look now at page 11 of this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, you have drawn a number 2, 3, 4, and 5 on the right-hand corner of the map. Is it correct that these depict the different locations of the graves that were dug at the base, at the firing range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K88
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we briefly go into private session for a couple of questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this to protect the security of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We'll no longer be referring to page 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Page 10452-10454 Private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of February, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24
